newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends below support, ACCESS up on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends below support, ACCESS up on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by a late wave of long liquidation, closed below support Wednesday, then rallied slightly on ACCESS after a weekly AGA stock report at the low end of expectations.
July skidded 5.1 cents to close at $2.071 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.109 on ACCESS after the inventory data. August settled 4.8 cents lower at $2.107.

"Ninety-one (bcf stock build) is a pretty big number, but we've had zero weather, and it easily could have been triple digits. I think we rally a little from here. It's a little early to give up on summer," said one Midwest trader.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 91 bcf, at the low end of the 90-100 bcf expected range, and were still 220 bcf, or 21 percent, above year-ago.

Eastern storage, which gained 59 bcf last week, was 104 bcf, or 20 percent, over last year. Producing region stocks rose 21 bcf and remained almost 60 percent above 1996 levels. Western inventories continued to lag year-ago by 14 percent.
While technical traders said July's break of support Wednesday could set up a test of the $2 area, others saw little reason for prices to move far in either direction.
July resistance was seen first at $2.21, then at $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high at $2.44.

More seasonal weather is forecast for the Midwest and Northeast by the weekend and expected to last into next week. The Southeast also was expected to be mostly normal, with Florida climbing to above-normal levels.
In the cash, swing gas in the Louisiana Gulf was unchanged Wednesday in the mid-teens. Midcon pipes also held steady in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was flat at about $2.43.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip tumbled 3.3 cents to $2.196. NYMEX said 34,904 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 30,482.

On the KCBT, July finished 3.7 cents lower at $1.948, while deferreds ended down by one-half to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 12.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 336 lots traded, down from Tuesday's total of 520.
